I was playing a little CSGO earlier today just chilling out, and the idea occurred to me about having a regular gaming tournament, like a league of teams/leaderboard, where we can organize teams of players and compete against each other, score points based on winners, host it over a month or two, and the top team receives some sort of prize (or possibly then go head-to-head for an ultimate winner and have runner up prizes). For example, /u/Razzy posted a couple days ago about giving away a copy of The Witcher 3 - (props to you Razz for the surprise spontaneous giveaway) - and just from the link, you can see the interest that it drummed up (over 100 responses, albeit some of them general comments and chatter, but still). For runner up teams, something like user flairs for the team's placement comes to mind, or codes to less high-profile games etc. I imagine that the platform of choice would be PC (I think it's accurate to say that's what most people here play on), but we could easily livestream the rounds to Twitch or YouTube for them to watch, and for record of the games (I could imagine memorable moments that shift the round completely etc).

Depending on how people feel about it, we could also have the option of a low cost entry fee, to either put towards the chosen prize, or to make the cash pool for the winning team (obviously a little more complicated with splitting and sending funds, but still possible). I also remember something a while back about us all sharing any extra games we have keys for (I think the example it had was like spare keys from Humble Bundles and the like), so that's also an option.

There's only a couple downsides that I could foresee possibly happening. Firstly, ensuring that attendance is actually happening. Obviously, planning ahead and discussing times people can play (and possibly issues with timezones). I know of the official /v/gaming Steam group, and the lack of love it gets, but if there was an actual prize at the end of the league/season, it might be enough of an incentive for people to play together regularly enough that we could host games.

Secondly, accessibility. For example, I was playing it pretty lax earlier, but everybody is aware of the competitive nature that surrounds CSGO, which on the one hand would make it quite a good example of a game to host a competition over. However, the fear of a difference in skill level might be enough to deter people's enthusiasm for continuing, or even throwing their name into the hat to participate. Whilst we could do our best to balance the teams and skills, it might be easier to play more "friendly" games that don't have such a clear and distinct difference in skill are easier to get into, such as Rocket League, or to ensure that everybody can get hold of the chosen title, possibly a free-to-play game. Obviously, this is just my own speculation, everybody could be fine with CSGO for example, just throwing it out there.

So, well, I'm just wondering what your opinion is on any of this :P Do you think it's feasible? Are you interested in participating? Do you want to help? Do you want to help with organizing but have no interest in participating? Do you think it's a terrible idea? Do you have a different game suggestion? I'm going to bed (it's already past midnight here), but I've been throwing the idea around in my mind this afternoon, and I'm curious as to hear what other people think.

Cheers,

Vansen
